checkpoints.description: [1/6] Plan: zero-dependency Pebble language v1. Frozen surface (recorded in ADR-001 with milestone 1): values int/float/bool/string/list plus none as the absence of a value; statements let, assignment, if/else, while, for-in, fn, return, blocks; operators + - * / % ^, comparisons, and/or/not, calls, indexing, list literals; builtins print, len, range, str, int, floor, min, max, abs; interfaces: file runner, -e, REPL; exit codes 0/1/2; every lexer, parser and runtime error renders file:line:col with Why and Fix. Non-goals: classes, modules, closures, exceptions, unicode identifiers, break/continue, slices, script arguments. Slice boundaries adjusted from the draft so each slice is complete in itself, never a stub: [1] plan, scaffold, ADR-001 and lexer; [2] parser and AST; [3] evaluator core with control flow, functions and return; [4] the nine builtins and value formatting; [5] CLI, REPL, examples and README demo; [6] hardening, error-format meta test, platform and perf guards, Phase 4. Executing milestone 1 now: failing-first lexer tests written; implementation next.

impact_assessment.why: The hardest-to-fake test of AIKit's governance available: hundreds of objective semantics tests, dozens of error paths that must obey the Why/Fix contract, and maximal scope-creep temptation, so the plan, checkpoint and gate discipline itself is on trial. The result is also a small interpreter later projects can embed as a rules engine.
impact_assessment.benefits: A green run demonstrates the gates catch semantics, error-quality and platform defects, and that feature-freeze plus M<=6 discipline holds. The user gains a fully owned, dependency-free mini-language with a REPL, examples and a sub-10-second demo.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: the v1 surface must be frozen by ADR-001 or it grows without bound; grammar and truthiness choices are contracts pinned by tests. dependency: none, standard library only (pathlib, dataclasses, sys, difflib). concurrency: none, single-threaded, no state files, no locks. state: nothing persisted; the interpreter is stateless. platform: explicit UTF-8 reads with BOM tolerance, CRLF tolerance, pathlib only.
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-001 written before semantics; failing-first tests per slice; an error-format meta test in [6/6] proving every error carries file:line:col plus Why and Fix; a perf sanity test; aikit check pebble as Phase 4 before every commit; recursion, type and division failures surface as Pebble errors, never Python tracebacks.

checkpoints.description: [1/6] complete: scaffold (pyproject, package, tests package), ADR-001 language-surface freeze, and the lexer with 18 green tests (token streams, positions, CRLF, escapes, comments, error paths). ADR-001 records none as the absence of a value; README filled truthfully so the guidelines gate passes. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [2/6] parser and AST.

[2/6] complete: the AST (nodes.py, frozen, every node positioned) and the recursive-descent parser (precedence chain, right-associative power, else-if chains, single-comparison rule, trailing-comma hints, parse-depth guard). 45 tests green; the failing-first run caught one real defect (expression-leading keywords not/true/false/none rejected as statements) which was fixed before green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [3/6] evaluator core with control flow, functions and return.

[3/6] complete: the evaluator (scopes and scope rules, full operator set with typed error messages, truthiness, short-circuit and/or, if/else, while, for-in, functions, recursion capped at 100 calls, return unwinding, list/string indexing with negative offsets, unknown-name suggestions via difflib, division/power guards, and a deep-chain RecursionError converted into a positioned Pebble error). 85 tests green (40 new evaluator tests). aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [4/6] the nine builtins and value formatting.

[4/6] complete: the nine builtins (print, len, range, str, int, floor, min, max, abs) in stdlib.py with arity metadata, strict argument rules and positioned EvalErrors; shared value formatting (true/false, none, escaped quoted strings inside lists, <fn>/<builtin> names, float display) in formatting.py; builtins seeded into the global scope and suggested by the unknown-name fixer. ADR-002 fixes builtin semantics and the display form. 24 new failing-first builtin tests; 109 tests green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [5/6] CLI, REPL, examples and README demo.

[5/6] complete: the CLI (file runner, -e/--eval, piped stdin, --help, --version), exit codes 0/1/2, UTF-8 BOM/CRLF file reads and Why/Fix usage reports; the stateful REPL with multi-line continuation, non-none value echo, error recovery and end-of-file reporting; python -m pebble plus a console-script entry point; three runnable examples (hello, fizzbuzz, fibonacci) and a sub-10-second README demo. 15 new failing-first CLI/REPL tests; 124 tests green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [6/6] hardening, error-format meta test, platform and perf guards, Phase 4.

[6/6] complete: hardening (v1 caps for int size, exponents, ranges and sequences; finite float literals; zero-to-negative-power and float-overflow division become positioned errors; CLI internal-error shield so no host traceback escapes), the error-format meta test over lexer/parser/runtime corpora, CRLF and unicode platform tests, and 50k-loop/10k-statement perf guards. ADR-003 records the limits. 18 new tests; 142 tests green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Task complete.

[1/4] break and continue end-to-end: ADR-004, lexer keywords, AST nodes, parser loop-context validation (a fn body is not a loop context), evaluator signals caught by the innermost while or for, failing-first tests; [2/4] slices end-to-end: Slice AST, parser start:stop[:step], evaluator with int bounds, bool refusal, zero-step refusal and Python-style negative/clamped bounds, tests; [3/4] range(start, stop, step) and the float() builtin, with arity, type, zero-step and non-finite guards, tests; [4/4] README and decisions cross-check, regenerated codebase map, full aikit check pebble, delivery

impact_assessment.why: v1 is complete and green (142 tests, 4/4 gates), and ADR-001 names break/continue, slices and float() as deferred conveniences while ADR-002 records the missing range step as a cost; the next bounded increment makes early-exit loops, subsequences and text-to-float conversion possible without reopening the rest of the frozen surface
impact_assessment.benefits: scripts can stop a loop early, skip an iteration, take a list or string subsequence, count with a step and convert numeric text to a float; each addition is pinned by failing-first tests and keeps the existing positioned Why/Fix error contract
impact_assessment.risks: contract: a v2 surface change, so ADR-004 must amend ADR-001 and ADR-002 and every new failure must keep the three-line error format; dependency: standard library only (re for the float string grammar); concurrency: none, the interpreter is single-threaded and persists no state; state: no files, locks or schemas change
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests per feature; parser rejects break/continue outside a loop and resets loop context inside fn bodies; slices delegate to Python semantics and pin them; the hardening error corpora gain the new parse and runtime paths; run aikit check pebble and record checklists before every commit; README updated in the same commit as each user-visible feature

checkpoints.description: [1/4] complete: ADR-004 records the whole v2 surface; break/continue keywords, AST nodes, parser loop-context rules (fn body resets the context, errors point at the keyword) and evaluator signals caught by the innermost while or for; 9 failing-first tests (1 lexer, 4 parser, 4 evaluator); 151 tests green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [2/4] slices.

[2/4] complete: ':' token; Slice AST node and the start:stop[:step] subscript parser with a three-part error; evaluator slices lists and strings with int-only bounds (bools refused), a zero-step refusal and Python-style negative/clamped parts; hardening corpora gain the new parse and runtime paths; 9 failing-first tests (3 parser, 6 evaluator) plus 4 corpus entries; 160 tests green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [3/4] range with a step and float().

[3/4] complete: range accepts range(start, stop, step) with int-only arguments, a zero-step refusal and the same 1,000,000-value cap; float() converts ints, floats and strictly decimal strings, refuses bools, whitespace, non-decimal text and non-finite results, and turns an int beyond the float range into an EvalError; 6 new failing-first builtin tests plus 2 hardening corpus entries; 166 tests green. aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [4/4] final docs, map and verification.

[4/4] complete: README tree, status and v2 wording align with the code; codebase map regenerated; full aikit check pebble run: 4/4 gates (test 166 green, hygiene, guidelines, secrets); checklists: passed. Task complete.

[1/3] ADR-005 and evaluator core: Interpreter(out=None, args=None) seeds global 'args' list of strings (defaults to []), friendly fix when attempting to call args(), failing-first evaluator tests; [2/3] CLI and runner integration: parse arguments after FILE, -e SOURCE, stdin -, and -- option terminator, passing string args to Interpreter; update test_cli.py with failing-first CLI argument tests; [3/3] demo script in examples/, test_hardening corpora check, README updates, regenerated codebase map, full aikit check pebble, delivery

impact_assessment.why: Pebble scripts currently cannot access command-line arguments, limiting automation and scripting utility; adding script arguments via a global 'args' string list provides idiomatic CLI parameterization while keeping the language surface minimal and dependency-free
impact_assessment.benefits: Scripts can read arguments via 'args[0]', 'len(args)', slices, and for-in loops; CLI runner supports passing arguments after script path, -e code, and via stdin or '--' option delimiter; preserves the three-line positioned error contract
impact_assessment.risks: contract: language surface and CLI option parsing change, requiring ADR-005; dependency: standard library only; concurrency: none, single-threaded execution; state: no persistent state
impact_assessment.mitigation: ADR-005 recorded before code; backward-compatible Interpreter signature; failing-first tests per milestone; 100% test pass and full aikit check pebble gate before each commit

checkpoints.description: [1/3] complete: ADR-005 records script arguments contract; Interpreter(out=None, args=None) seeds global 'args' list with string args; calling args() provides helpful positioned error fix; 4 new failing-first evaluator tests (170 tests green). aikit check pebble: 4/4 gates; checklists: passed. Next: [2/3] CLI and runner integration.
